heroLead: The kingdom already showed up. It has not fully shown up. That gap is the room I write from, and it is also the room you live in on a Tuesday afternoon.
watchNote: Four to five clips a week, cut from what you already preached. Monday is the strongest hook from Sunday, Wednesday is a micro teaching, Friday is the human moment, Saturday answers something somebody actually asked.
watchPageNote: Church produced messages stay on the church’s channels and are embedded here, never re-hosted. Everything filmed independently lives on my own channel.
frameworksCaption: The top two bands are the standard picture: two ages, overlapping since the resurrection. The third band is Adrio König’s correction, and it is the one that changes how you preach it. The end is not a date at the far right of the line. It is a person running underneath the whole of it, for us at the cross, in us by the Spirit, with us at his coming. Time passing does not move you closer to the end, because the end is someone you are already in.
frameworksLead: This is the room BibleProject taught me to build, and König gave it a spine. He argued that treating eschatology as a chapter about the future eclipses Christ, who is himself the last thing. One framework a month: a diagram, an essay that walks it, a sixty second clip, and a one page guide people can take to their small group.
frameworksParked: Parked on purpose: the teaching archive. The notes are personal right now, and they should not go public until they are rewritten in a standard format another preacher could pick up and use.
readingTie: This is not a book review column. Whatever is on this shelf shows up in that week’s essay, the Monday note, or a clip. Readers get to watch an idea travel from a book into a sermon into a Tuesday.
kitNote: Every template is typography and your own photography, so nothing depends on borrowed images. The formats are the part that is culturally fluent: the two panel setup, the text thread, the burned in caption. Those read as native on Instagram and TikTok without borrowing anyone else’s picture.
